title: Main Analysis 1: The Pre-Announcement Run-Up

purpose.statement: Pay off H1 and the Section 2.4 MA1 single-indicator design by establishing claim C2: within firms, residual CEO Q&A uncertainty (UncResCEO) is elevated in the pre-announcement quarter of cash acquirers relative to their own other quarters, with the cash ratio rising on the same clock, while the stock-acquirer placebo shows no comparable positive run-up. Read strictly correlationally, within-firm, no identification. The formal cash-vs-stock difference is deferred to 3.4.
purpose.reason: 2.2 P2 stated H1 (theta_-1>0) and 2.4 P1 mapped the single-indicator design to it; the thesis needs the first empirical pillar (the run-up exists) before timing (3.3) and cash-specificity (3.4) can build on it. C2 is the ledger's rank-2 SOLID second pillar.
evidence: claim_findings_ledger.json C2 (rank 2; thinnest 'elevated for cash acquirers, not detectable for stock'; survives two-tailed p=.0074)
thesis_draft.tex 2.4 P1 (MA1 equation, beta estimates theta_-1, L94-98)

proposition_chain.statement: MA1 estimates the single-indicator two-way fixed-effects regression of Section 2.4 (firm and calendar year-quarter FE, firm-clustered SE) four times: each outcome (CashRatio, UncResCEO) in each arm (cash >=50%, stock >=50% placebo), with treated firms' post-announcement quarters dropped so the design observes only the run-up. Identification is within-firm (a treated firm's pre-announcement quarter against its own ordinary quarters); the estimating equation lives in 2.4 and is not restated.
proposition_chain.reason: Establishes the estimand (beta = theta_-1, a within-firm anticipation contrast) so the coefficients that follow have a defined meaning, while honoring the boundary that the equation belongs to 2.4.
evidence: variable_ledger.json tab:empire_building_did design (PanelOLS two-way FE, firm-clustered, post-announce dropped)

proposition_chain.statement: In the cash arm both clocks move in the final pre-announcement quarter: residual Q&A uncertainty is elevated and the cash ratio is rising (a coefficient that tracks the change in cash, not its level, because the cash equation carries the partial-adjustment lag). The residual coefficient survives a two-tailed test (p=.0074), so the table's one-tailed reporting convention does not drive the load-bearing result.
proposition_chain.reason: This is the core C2/H1 positive finding: the run-up is visible on the language clock with the cash clock corroborating. The two-tailed survival is load-bearing because the table prints one-tailed and a referee will check whether the result is an artifact of the convention; it is not.
evidence: thesis_draft.tex 2.4 P3.3 (CashRatio carries partial-adjustment lag; residual takes none)

proposition_chain.statement: The two cash-arm columns run on different universes because the residual exists only for CEOs with at least five calls: the uncertainty test (col 2) uses 27,622 firm-quarters of 1,248 firms while the cash-ratio test (col 1) uses 67,590 of 2,232; the uncertainty test is therefore the more demanding, smaller-universe one.
proposition_chain.reason: A referee will note the residual and cash columns are not the same sample; disclosing it pre-empts the criticism and explains the >=5-call selection (mechanic from 3.1, threat home 2.4 P5.5). These counts come from the empire_building_did N row, NOT from summary_stats panels.
numbers: 27,622 / 1,248 firms (cash UncResCEO universe, tab:empire_building_did col 2 N row)
67,590 / 2,232 firms (cash CashRatio universe, tab:empire_building_did col 1 N row)

proposition_chain.statement: The effect is material but modest: the uncertainty coefficient equals roughly fifteen percent of a residual standard deviation (about 15.3% on the all-universe basis), for a variable from which everything persistent has already been removed, in a quarter that is about one percent of the sample; the cash coefficient adds roughly half a percentage point of assets (about 3.0% of the mean cash ratio) to the cash stock in a single quarter. The SD basis is the live open decision and is surfaced, not silently picked.
proposition_chain.reason: Economic-magnitude reading turns the coefficient into a claim with stakes while keeping it honest (modest, on an already-purged variable). The denominators are sourced to live Table-1 cells; the stale old-draft pointers ('Table 1 Panel B 0.3072', '1.4% of sample', 'mean 0.1573 Panel A') are dropped.
evidence: claim_findings_ledger.json _sd_basis_note_2026_06_14 (dual-SD: 0.3010 all-universe vs 0.3072 estimation-sample; magnitude ~15% robust either way 15.0% vs 15.3%; old-draft 'Panel B' pointer stale)

proposition_chain.statement: The stock arm is the placebo: under the same disclosure constraint, with otherwise nearly identical models (the stock partial-adjustment lag 0.8013 is almost the same as the cash 0.7990), neither residual uncertainty (-0.0429, n.s.) nor the cash ratio (-0.0036, n.s.) shows a comparable positive run-up, so what differs at e=-1 is the response, not the model. A side-by-side reading is not yet a formal test of the difference; the formal cash-vs-stock test is supplied in Section 3.4 (Main Analysis 3).
proposition_chain.reason: Delivers the 'not detectable for stock' half of C2's thinnest claim; the near-identical lag rules out a model-difference explanation. The explicit deferral to 3.4 pre-empts the C6 Gelman-Stern trap of reading sig-vs-n.s. as the formal test.
evidence: claim_findings_ledger.json C6 risks (do NOT use side-by-side as the specificity test; Gelman-Stern)
numbers: 0.8013*** stock lag (tab:empire_building_did col 5, SE 0.0057) vs 0.7990*** cash lag (col 1)

coverage.purpose_fully_delivered: Complete. P1 sets the design/estimand (within-firm, no identification); P2 delivers the cash-arm run-up on both clocks with two-tailed survival (the C2 positive, H1 paid off); P3 discloses the two-universe N difference (from empire_building_did, not summary_stats); P4 gives the honest economic magnitude with denominators sourced to live Table-1 cells; P5 delivers the stock placebo and forward-links the formal difference to 3.4, sealing the Gelman-Stern trap. C2/H1 delivered exactly at the ledger ceiling: detectable for cash, not for stock, correlational and within-firm.
gaps: The formal cash-vs-stock difference is deliberately NOT claimed here (deferred to 3.4) -- bounded-by-design to avoid the Gelman-Stern fallacy
The SD-basis (and the parallel cash-mean basis) is left as a flagged open decision rather than resolved, per surface-not-solve

open_decisions: SD-basis for the ~15%-of-SD magnitude: estimation-sample 0.3072 (N=27,622, the UncResCEO-equation universe, with a footnote) OR all-universe Table-1 0.3010 (N=44,900). Magnitude ~15% robust either way (15.0% vs 15.3%). NOTE: the locked 2.5 prose already scales its FB percentages by the all-universe 0.300988, a coherence pull toward 0.3010; the old-draft 'Table 1 Panel B (0.3072)' pointer is doubly stale (the all-universe Table 1 has no Panel B reporting 0.3072 -- UncResCEO sits in Panel B at 0.3010). Pick ONE basis and apply consistently across 3.2/3.3/3.4.
Parallel cash-mean denominator basis: the old draft used a stale mean 0.1573 (Panel A); the live Table-1 mean CashRatio is 0.1708 (Panel C), giving 3.0% (was ~3.2%). Use 0.1708.
